newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Six workers have been arrested after the torching of a warehouse and head office of Sanyo Universal Electric Co on Tuesday night. As police tried to identify the ring leaders, the government moved swiftly to limit the damage the fire has caused to the investment climate. (BANGKOK POST)

- Chat Pattana Party leader Chatichai Choonhavan was found to be hospitalised yesterday amid a rumour that he suffering from the final stage of stomach cancer. The rumour circulated in the stock market throughout the day. Chatichai, also the government adviser, was found to have been admitted to Chulalongkorn Hospital where he was staying in room 2104, adjacent to the hospital's intensive care unit. (THE NATION)

- Draft legislation to create a powerful Election Commission was approved in principle by the House of Representatives yesterday. In a unanimous vote, MPs passed the draft, partly prepared by Pokin Polakul, a PM's Office minister, and to form an extraordinary scrutiny committee. (BANGKOK POST)

- The bonus row at Krung Thai Bank yesterday ended peacefully with the intervention of Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong and his deputy Chalerm Yubamrung. The government is likely to end up paying 125 million baht to help KTB meet its employees' bonus demand. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The torching of Sanyo Universal Plc's warehouse and head office by protesting employees has undermined Thailand's image as a production base for Japanese investors, the president of the Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) told The Nation. (THE NATION)

- Four key policies are to be followed by the Commerce Ministry in order to boost exports and maintain price stability, Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasenee announced yesterday. Narongchai said the ministry planned to retain existing markets and penetrate new ones, such as border areas, and Latin American and Eastern European countries, by assigning officers to build better trade relationships. (BUSINESS DAY)
